title: Selective digestion in a mixed milk-and-gelatin matrix
original_forecast: Lactase should act on the declared milk-sugar pool; protease should act on the declared gelatin-protein pool. The combined treatment should preserve separate material identities rather than report one generic digestion percentage.
original_limitations: The supported protein table does not make every milk protein a protease substrate. No enzyme competition, product inhibition or exact peptide chemistry is claimed.
lock_qualification: Producer-reported manifest hash; artifact omits raw Cargo.lock bytes.

assessment.hold_reason: Unexplained strict charge residual in combined arm; valid separate aggregate annotations do not waive the all-step inventory criterion.
assessment.model_scope: Separate milk lactose share (1.44 g) and gelatin protein share (0.45 g), not total milk mass, own the distinct annotations. Single-family controls and combined state retain identities; no exact molecular digestion products, competition or complete milk proteome model.

A reported pH or speciation therefore describes that proton-compensated analytical problem, not a prediction for a complete physical mixture of these ions. Supply the actual counterions or use complete acid, base or salt reagents; no sodium, chloride or other counterion is inferred
